title: Graph Document — Employees and Departments
description: Schema for the graph-document.json example (§8.12). Demonstrates TypeRefProperty relationships expressed via { "$ref-id": "..." } within a single graph document: Employee.department (has-one → Department) and Employee.manager (optional has-one → Employee, self-referential). Using $ref-id keeps objects independent (no embedding) while preserving full type validation — the validator resolves each $ref-id to its target object and validates it against the declared type.

Department.title: Department
Department.description: An organizational department. Exists independently — multiple Employees can reference the same Department.

Employee.title: Employee
Employee.description: An employee belonging to a Department. HAS-ONE (TypeRefProperty) → Department: in a graph document the value is expressed as { "$ref-id": "<dept-$id>" } instead of an inline embedded object, so the Department can be stored once and shared. Optional HAS-ONE (TypeRefProperty) → Employee (self-referential manager link).

department.description: HAS-ONE via TypeRefProperty: in a graph document this property holds { "$ref-id": "<dept-$id>" } instead of an inline embedded Department. The validator resolves the reference and validates the target against the Department type definition.

manager.description: Optional HAS-ONE via TypeRefProperty (self-referential): the employee's direct manager, expressed as a $ref-id reference in the graph document.
